content: CSMN Frequently Asked Questions Who is CSMN? CSMN stands for Chinese Student Ministries Netherlands. We are a Christian organization for Chinese students and are officially linked to the International Christian Fellowship (ICF). What do we do? We create a safe and welcoming space where students can explore faith, ask meaningful questions, build community, and grow together. This includes regular meetings, discussions, worship, social events, and occasional trips or retreats. What do we not do? We do not force anyone to follow Jesus. We respect everyone's journey and beliefs. Why specifically Chinese students? Our team has a special bond with China. Most of us have lived there and feel a deep connection to the culture and people. We want Chinese students to feel seen, understood, and at home in a country that can feel very different from their own. I am not a Christian. Can I join? Yes. We welcome students from all backgrounds and worldviews, whether you are curious, skeptical, or simply want to explore faith and ask big questions. What is the cost for membership? There is no cost to join. Our events and meetings are free unless otherwise specified for special events or trips. What can I expect? We aim for a friendly and respectful environment. We do not drink alcohol or smoke during our gatherings or events. What kind of activities do we do besides the regular meetings? In addition to weekly gatherings, we organize: Hikes and nature trips Movie nights Social dinners Game nights Weekend retreats and camps What does a typical evening look like? A usual evening includes: Welcome and informal hangout Singing or worship, with optional participation A short talk or discussion Group conversation or reflection Food, snacks, and social time Are you only for Protestants? While we are a Protestant Christian organization, we warmly welcome students from all denominations and beliefs. Everyone is invited to join and be part of the community.

content: Welcome to Chinese Student Ministries Netherlands (CSMN) CSMN is a community for Chinese university students in the Netherlands, with a special focus on those living and studying in Wageningen. We provide a welcoming and open space where students can connect, build friendships, and explore meaningful questions about life, culture, and faith. What We Offer In addition to our weekly fellowship gatherings, where we share a Chinese meal and engage in discussions guided by the Bible, we also organize a wide range of events throughout the year. These events are designed to be both thoughtful and enjoyable, because life is serious, but also fun! Examples of past and upcoming activities include: BBQs & Hot Pot evenings Cross cultural exchange nights "Life Explored" sessions Leadership development workshop Hikes in and around Wageningen Chestnut picking in autumn City trips to explore the Netherlands And many more! Whether you are looking for a place to grow personally, spiritually, or socially, you are warmly invited to join us. Find out more about our events here! content: Bible study Christian faith is expressed in many different ways, and these forms and practices are often treated as if they are opposing each other, each claiming to define the Christian faith itself. For someone new to Christianity, this can lead to confusion and questions. There is no simple explanation for the diversity among Christian churches. Even if we study every distinction and attempt to reconcile opposing viewpoints, complete unity will remain out of reach. The world is simply too diverse, and human nature—with its desire for uniqueness and its inherent stubbornness—makes complete unity impossible. Fortunately, within this great diversity there are a few core shared convictions. These common foundations are expressed profoundly in the Apostles’ Creed, which summarizes the core beliefs Christians around the world affirm. While different traditions may place varying emphasis on certain themes, there remains a broad and enduring agreement on the essential truths of the faith and the need to hold these central convictions in common. To appreciate the harmony within this diversity, we must look for deeper truth: the truth that God’s love can shine through every unique context. At CSMN, we invite our participants to explore the richness and variety found in different Christian traditions. We understand these expressions as contextual manifestations of God’s love in the world. The way God’s love appeared 8,000 years ago is not identical to how it is expressed in the 21st century. Yet the love of God itself has never changed; His passion for humanity remains the same. Scripture preserves these expressions of God’s love for us. The stories of how God interacted with people throughout history have been gathered into the canon of the Hebrew Bible and the New Testament. This canon is closed and has remained stable, serving as the foundational reference for Christians for nearly 2,000 years. Because the Bible is our core “textbook,” we place strong emphasis on studying it. Through Scripture, we learn how God has revealed Himself across the centuries and how earlier generations came to know Him. We intentionally anchor our thinking in the revelation God has already given. The materials you will find on our site are used in one way or another. Some were written by us, and others were borrowed. We will mention the source and link to the original or to the place where you can purchase it. Online Bible Commentaries A commentary on the Bible—or on a specific biblical book—is a collection of articles written by scholars or thoughtful readers who offer insight into the text. Commentaries provide fresh perspectives and often address questions such as who wrote the material, when it was written, and for what purpose. They expound the meaning of the text for its original audience and help us understand how those insights apply to our contemporary lives. Because there is a long history—spanning thousands of years—of biblical commentaries, choosing reliable ones is important. Below, you will find materials we have used in the past or still use when appropriate. Traditional Commentaries We understand traditional Bible commentaries as focused explanations of the Bible written by a specific author to expound and provide meaning for daily life. Unlike comprehensive study tools that cover the entire Bible with a wide variety of features, these commentaries provide a more concentrated look at the text. They often provide basic historical background, theological reflection, and verse by verse insight. The focus is more on preaching and on what it means to surrender to Jesus. Use this material to quickly get an impression of what a certain passage entails. These tools typically include a wide range of resources—such as study notes, articles, maps, timelines, word studies, and thematic guides—to help readers understand the Bible from multiple angles. Many of these resources are now available online, providing quick access to extensive libraries of information and allowing for deeper, more integrated study. Because they draw from numerous voices and perspectives, whole Bible study tools are especially valuable for gaining a well rounded understanding of Scripture. content: The Gospel The entire Bible centers on a single, surprisingly simple theme: God loves you so much that He made a way to be forgiven for every sin, so you can spend eternity with Him. That’s the essence of the gospel, and the central subject of the Scriptures. The written Word of God is intended to help us understand this “good news.” By studying the Bible, we learn that each person needs to be saved (Romans 3:23), each person can be saved (Romans 1:16), and God wants each person to be saved (2 Peter 3:9). What separates us from God is sin. No matter how good we think we are, every person is guilty of sin (1 John 1:10). Since God is absolutely perfect, no one deserves to spend eternity in heaven. Instead, we deserve to be separated from Him forever (Romans 5:16). No amount of effort, no good deeds, no money, no talent, no achievements are enough to take away this guilt (Isaiah 64:6). Fortunately, God doesn’t want us to be separated from Him, so He made a way to fix what’s broken (John 3:16 17). That one and only way is through faith in Jesus Christ (John 14:6). God Himself came to earth, as a human, living a perfect and sinless life (Hebrews 4:15). He willingly died as a sacrifice to pay the debt for our sins (2 Corinthians 5:21). According to the Scriptures, anyone can be “saved”—forgiven by God and guaranteed heaven—through faith in Jesus Christ (Romans 10:13). This isn’t a call for blind, ignorant belief (Acts 17:11; 1 John 4:1). It’s an invitation from the Holy Spirit to submission and trust (James 4:7). It’s a choice to let go of everything else in order to rely entirely on God. There is nothing anyone can “do” in order to be saved. The only way a person can find salvation is by accepting Jesus Christ as their Savior. This simply means believing that… I am a sinner, who deserves God’s judgment (Romans 3:23; Romans 6:23). Jesus Christ is God, and He came to earth as a man (John 1:14). Jesus died, in my place, in order to pay for my sins (Romans 8:3 4; Hebrews 10:14). Jesus came back from the dead, as He said He would (Romans 4:25; Mark 8:31). I am trusting in Jesus’ sacrifice, and nothing else, in order to save me (Ephesians 2:8 9; John 3:5). As best I know how, I am turning away from my sins, putting all of my faith (trust) in Jesus to save me (2 Corinthians 7:10; Acts 16:31). That’s it! Anyone who truly believes those things is forgiven, changed from the inside out (James 1:18; 2 Corinthians 5:17), and destined for heaven. The gospel is simple enough for anyone to understand (Matthew 18:13), but very difficult for people to accept (Romans 1:20 21). The truth of the gospel means we are not perfect. We are not in total control of our lives (Psalm 39:5). We cannot save ourselves. We need something “more” than us to make things right (1 Thessalonians 4:8). Becoming a Christian is not about being better than others. The gospel is for those who admit they are weak and need to be rescued (2 Corinthians 12:9). That’s a hard truth, but everything we learn from the Bible proves this truth. Each theme explored in Scripture points towards this gospel message of sin, redemption, and salvation through faith. It’s the most important decision a person will ever make: do I accept what God offers, or do I turn my back on it (Matthew 7:13)? Which one will you choose (2 Corinthians 6:2)? I just became a Christian! Now that I've put my faith in Jesus, what do I do now? Wonderful! Trusting in Christ is absolutely the best and most important decision anyone can ever make (John 3:16–18; Titus 3:4–7). It's also the start of a lifelong process of growth and learning. That journey is not always easy (John 16:33), but God promises to help us along the way (Matthew 28:20; John 14:18). If you want to speak with someone about this decision, or if you have other questions about trusting Christ as your Savior, you can click here to start a live chat. Please read the information in the article below. If you have questions about your decision or would like to share something about it, there are two ways you can do so. One is through our primary ministry page, at https://www.gotquestions.org/Bible Questions.html. The other way is sending us an email at contact@bibleref.com. Take advantage of our Church Finder page, so you can locate a solid Bible teaching church in your area. I just became a Christian! Now that I've put my faith in Jesus, what do I do now? Congratulations! Accepting Christ as your Savior not only changes your eternity (John 3:36), it changes your life! However, it doesn't instantly answer all possible questions. You may be wondering " what am I supposed to do now? How do I follow God now that I've trusted in Jesus ?" Here are five basic ideas you can use to get started. If you find something confusing or concerning, don't forget to check our commentary here at BibleRef.com, or the vast resources available at GotQuestions.org. 1) Be sure you understand your decision for salvation. Scripture tells us it's possible to know whether we've truly been saved (1 John 5:13). That serves two purposes. First, it gives us reassurance, comforting us with a reminder that we're eternally redeemed. Second, it gives us a way to recognize if we're not quite there, yet. The basic outline of salvation, as given in Scripture, is this: a) Everyone has sinned; every person has done things which disobey and displease God (Romans 3:23). b) God is perfectly good and holy, so our sin separates us from Him. We deserve to be eternally disconnected from Him (Romans 6:23). c) Out of love and mercy, God came in the form of Jesus Christ, who died to pay the penalty we owe for our sin (Romans 5:8; 2 Corinthians 5:21). By dying on the cross, Jesus took the punishment we deserve. By rising from the dead, Jesus proved His message was true, and that His death covers our debt of sin. d) Anyone who trusts in the death of Christ as payment for their sins is granted forgiveness—salvation—from God. Those who admit their sin, sincerely relying on Jesus for salvation, will be saved (John 3:16; Romans 5:1; Romans 8:1). That means an eternity in heaven. e) Those who have been saved are immediately, and permanently, given the Holy Spirit (John 14:26). The Spirit helps us to learn God's truth, through the Bible, and gives us the power to live accordingly. Those are the core points of the gospel. If you place your faith in Christ, as your Savior, then you are saved, right now! That means God will never abandon you or turn away from you (Romans 8:38–39; Matthew 28:20). A person who is genuinely saved cannot lose that salvation—ever (John 10:28–29). If you have accepted Christ, you can be confident in your salvation and rely on His power to follow God's will. 2) Connect with a Bible teaching Church. The primary purposes of a Christian church are fellowship, teaching of the Bible, and worship. Being connected to a local church is not merely a good idea: it's a command from God (Hebrews 10:25). God never intended for people to be entirely alone (Genesis 2:18). He also does not intend for Christians to be alone in their spiritual lives (Ephesians 4:15–16; 1 Corinthians 12:19–20). And so, the local church is important. The church , in this case, is not the building but the people who serve and associate with each other. The simple concept of being together—sharing time and space—is called fellowship . We need other believers to help us properly understand the written Word of God (Acts 8:30–31; Titus 1:7–9). Newer believers need the wisdom and experience of more mature Christians (Titus 2:1). This process is called discipleship . Discipleship is crucial to living a successful Christian life. The Bible is our ultimate guide (2 Timothy 3:16–17; 1 Corinthians 4:6), but mentors and friends are necessary to properly grasp those truths (Proverbs 11:14; Hebrews 5:12–14). Churches are also important so that followers of Christ can thank God for all He has done for us. This act of praising God is called worship . Because God is holy, merciful, loving, righteous and gracious, He deserves our worship (Revelation 4:11; Isaiah 6:1–7). 3) Take time for God on a daily basis. For a saved Christian, contact with God is like food: the longer one goes without, the weaker one becomes. It's critical for a believer to spend time focused on God, every single day. Some people carve out a set time in their schedule for this, often called quiet time or a daily devotion . Whether this is in the morning or evening, at a routine time or at different moments, it does not matter. What's important is that you commit to daily, prioritized time alone with God every day. That usually takes one of two forms: The first way we focus on God is prayer. Prayer does not have to be long, complicated, or eloquent. It does not have to use the "right" words or be organized in the "right" way. Jesus' model prayer (Matthew 6:9–13) tells us that prayer is where we praise God, tell Him what concerns us, and ask Him to provide for those needs. The second way is study of the Word of God: the Bible. Teachers and pastors in a church will help you learn about Scripture. However, it's very important to read the Bible yourself. Scripture is the most authoritative source of spiritual knowledge. While it does not answer every question a person could possibly ask, it does tell us everything we must know to live according to God's will. 4) Develop relationships for spiritual growth. Being involved with a local church is important. What's also important is connecting to individual people, on a personal level. The people you choose to spend time with will have a massive influence on your life: their approach to spiritual things will "rub off" on you. While that doesn't mean we should cut all non believers out of our lives, it does mean we need to prioritize relationships with those who love and honor God. Christian relationships include simple friendship, where two people encourage each other, provide support, and even accountability. It also includes mentorship, where a more spiritually mature believer helps a less mature Christian grow in their faith. The more time you spend living, serving, and communicating with other Christians, the more secure your faith will be. 5) Follow God's will and be Baptized. This step is last on the list only because it is often over emphasized. Baptism is not a requirement for salvation. Nor is it a magic ritual which physically washes away sins. Baptism is a public step of obedience: it's a way of declaring your faith in Christ. To be baptized—from a term meaning "to immerse in water"—is to symbolically identify with the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ (Romans 6:3–4). It's the first and primary step of obedience which each saved person is called to follow. If you have sincerely and legitimately accepted Christ as your Savior, you should speak with the pastor of your local church about being baptized. Source: The Gospel | BibleRef.com and Now what? | BibleRef.com Testimony Writing and Sharing Writing a Christian testimony is a meaningful way to share the story of your personal journey with God. It’s not a requirement found in Scripture, but it is a useful tool that can help you communicate your faith to others, whether during evangelism, a public baptism, or simply sharing your testimony with friends and family. By writing your testimony, you can reflect on your spiritual journey and how Christ has transformed your life. This exercise can also encourage new believers, giving them confidence in sharing their faith story. Below is a practical guide for writing your personal testimony. Once you complete it in English, review it with a Bible teacher for clarity. Afterward, translate it into your native language and create a document with two columns, one for each language. Be sure to include your first name, the date, and the year. You can use this document to help you share your personal faith story with others or for your own memorization. Background Where and how was I raised (culturally, socially, spiritually, and politically) What was my perception of life and death? What did I know about Christianity? Conversion process What made me decide to investigate the Bible, the God of the Bible, and Christianity? When and where was that? What convinced me that the God of the Bible is real and how did it happen that I accepted the Bible as God’s true Word? What role did Jesus have in this? Bible verses? What does sin mean to me? Do I need forgiveness of my sins and why? How do I confess my sins? What are the Bible verses that helped me understand? What is repentance to me? Do I want to change direction and how? Who is the owner of my life? Which Bible verses are leading in that process? Why do I want or not (yet) want to get baptized? Mention Bible verses if applicable. My new status, worldview, and expectations Who is Jesus for me? Give Bible verses. Who is the Holy Spirit and where is He in my life? What is my new role in relationships? Think about family, friends, intimacy (dating/marriage), church, society (worldview), etc. What is my destiny in eternity? Bible verses. For what am I grateful to God? Testimony Sharing For some people, sharing their testimony feels natural. For others, sharing 'your life story' is more challenging. When you are prepared, it is easier to share and make a difference. Below are a few simple tips to help you get started: 1. Reflect on these five questions Take some time to think through your story by answering these key questions: Who were you before you got to know Jesus? How did you come to know Him? What happened when you chose to receive His forgiveness? How has your life changed since then? What impact does your faith have on your life today? 2. Keep it simple You don’t need to include every detail. Start by writing down what comes to mind. You can always expand or refine your story later. 3. Prepare different versions Try creating a 30 minute, 15 minute, and 5 minute version of your testimony. This helps you stay clear and focused, no matter how much time you have to share. Above all, remember: this is your story. Be honest, be real, and let it reflect who you are. How do I get saved? This question supposes the need for being saved. If you don’t have that question, feel free to read more elsewhere on our site. The foundation of Christianity is that salvation is only through faith in Jesus as Savior. The one thing you must do in order to get right with God is to accept this truth: Jesus did everything necessary to restore the relationship between you and God. It is not more complicated than that. However, the positive implication is huge! Basically, God has done His part already. He has stretched out His hand, and you can grasp it to be lifted out of misery. He will then give you a true identity and personhood, and you will be changed in your thinking. In this new identity, you are a new creation while still being completely yourself. You will become the real you. This new you will act differently because you have new hope and a new reason to live. Your current habits will all be brought before God. Some habits might be refined because they are gifts from the Spirit. Other habits you might want to let go of because they are not healthy. You will also begin to do good works. Where your life was previously centered on yourself, you will become selfless. This does not mean you will never have time for yourself, but your time with others will be focused on their good and well being. This goes further than just responding to situations. You will find new ways to serve God and your community. There are good works that God provides for you to do. Good works are part of the new life God gives. People who do not understand the Christian faith often ask: if you only have to believe, then can you continue doing bad things? So who is that Christian God anyway? To answer this question, we will give you some direction on how the Bible speaks about this: This is perhaps the most important question in all of Christian theology. This question is the cause of the Reformation, the split between the Protestant churches and the Roman Catholic Church. Is salvation by faith alone, or by faith plus works? Am I saved just by believing in Jesus, or do I have to believe in Jesus and do certain things? There are some hard to reconcile Bible passages. Compare Romans 3:28, 5:1 and Galatians 3:24 with James 2:24. Some see a difference between Paul (salvation is by faith alone) and James (salvation is by faith plus works). Paul dogmatically says that justification is by faith alone (Ephesians 2:8 9), while James appears to be saying that justification is by faith plus works (James 2:17 18). This apparent problem is answered by examining what exactly James is talking about. James is refuting the belief that a person can have faith without producing any good works. James is emphasizing the point that genuine faith in Christ will produce a changed life and good works (James 2:20 26). James is not saying that justification is by faith plus works, but rather that a person who is truly justified by faith will have good works in his/her life. If a person claims to be a believer but has no good works in his/her life, then he/she likely does not have genuine faith in Christ (James 2:14, 17, 20, 26). Paul says the same thing in his writings. The good fruit believers should have in their lives is listed in Galatians 5:22 23. Immediately after telling us that we are saved by faith, not works (Ephesians 2:8 9), Paul informs us that we were created to do good works (Ephesians 2:10). Paul expects just as much of a changed life as James does: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has gone, the new is here! (2 Corinthians 5:17). James and Paul do not disagree in their teaching regarding salvation. They approach the same subject from different perspectives. Paul simply emphasized that justification is by faith alone while James put the emphasis on the fact that genuine faith in Christ produces good works.

content: CSMN 常见问题 CSMN 是谁？ CSMN 是 Chinese Student Ministries Netherlands 的缩写。我们是面向中国学生的基督教组织，并正式与 International Christian Fellowship (ICF) 有联系。 我们做什么？ 我们提供一个安全、欢迎人的空间，让学生可以探索信仰、提出重要问题、建立群体并一起成长。内容包括定期聚会、讨论、敬拜、社交活动，以及偶尔的旅行或退修。 我们不做什么？ 我们不会强迫任何人跟随耶稣。我们尊重每个人的旅程和信念。 为什么特别面向中国学生？ 我们的团队与中国有特别的连接。我们中许多人曾经在中国生活，对中国文化和人有深厚的感情。我们希望中国学生在一个与家乡很不同的国家里，仍然感到被理解、被看见、有归属感。 我不是基督徒，可以参加吗？ 可以。无论你来自什么背景、持有什么世界观，只要你愿意探索信仰、提出问题或认识朋友，都欢迎你参加。 会员费用是多少？ 参加 CSMN 没有会员费。除非特别活动或旅行另有说明，我们的聚会和活动都是免费的。 我可以期待什么？ 我们努力营造友好、尊重的环境。在聚会和活动中，我们不饮酒，也不吸烟。 除了固定聚会，还有什么活动？ 除了每周聚会，我们还会组织： 徒步和自然活动 电影之夜 社交晚餐 游戏之夜 周末退修和营会 一个典型的晚上是什么样？ 通常会包括： 欢迎和自由交流 唱诗或敬拜，参与是自愿的 简短分享或讨论 小组对话或反思 食物、点心和社交时间 CSMN 只面向新教徒吗？ 我们是一个新教基督教组织，但欢迎来自各种教派、背景和信念的学生加入群体。

content: 圣经学习 基督信仰在许多不同传统和实践中被表达出来，有时这些形式看起来彼此相对，好像各自都在定义什么才是真正的基督信仰。对刚接触基督信仰的人来说，这可能带来困惑和问题。基督教会之间的多样性并没有简单的解释。即使我们研究每一个区别，并尝试调和不同观点，完全一致仍然不容易达到。世界本来就非常多元，而人性中对独特性的渴望和固执，也使完全合一变得困难。 幸运的是，在这种多样性中，仍然有一些共同的核心信念。这些共同基础在《使徒信经》中有深刻表达，它总结了世界各地基督徒所认信的核心信仰。不同传统可能强调不同主题，但在信仰的基本真理上仍有广泛而持久的共识，也需要共同持守这些中心信念。 若要欣赏这种多样性中的和谐，我们需要寻找更深的真理：上帝的爱可以在每一个独特处境中发光。在 CSMN，我们邀请参与者探索不同基督教传统中的丰富性和多样性。我们把这些表达理解为上帝之爱在世界中的处境化彰显。上帝的爱在很久以前的表达方式，不一定与二十一世纪的表达方式相同；但上帝的爱本身从未改变，他对人的热情仍然一样。 圣经保存了上帝爱我们的这些表达。上帝如何在历史中与人互动的故事，被收集在希伯来圣经和新约圣经的正典中。这个正典已经完成，并一直稳定地成为近两千年来基督徒的根本参考。 因为圣经是我们的核心“教材”，我们非常重视学习圣经。通过圣经，我们认识上帝如何在历史中启示自己，也认识前人如何认识他。我们有意识地把自己的思想扎根在上帝已经赐下的启示中。 你在我们网站上看到的材料，会以不同方式被使用。有些是我们自己写的，有些是借用或推荐的。我们会尽量注明来源，并链接到原始资料或可以购买的地方。 在线圣经注释 圣经注释是关于圣经或某一卷圣经书卷的文章集合，由学者或认真思考的读者写成，帮助人理解经文。注释提供新的视角，也常常处理一些问题，例如作者是谁、写作时间、写作目的，以及经文对最初读者的意义和对今天生活的应用。由于圣经注释有很长的历史，选择可靠资料很重要。下面列出的是我们过去使用过，或在合适时候仍会使用的材料。 传统注释 传统圣经注释通常是由某一位作者写成的集中解释，帮助读者理解圣经经文，并思考它对日常生活的意义。不同于涵盖整本圣经、功能很多的综合学习工具，这些注释更专注于文本本身，常常提供基本历史背景、神学反思和逐节解释。它们更偏向讲道和思考什么是降服于耶稣。 这些材料可以帮助你快速了解某段经文的大意。 作者 / 名称 内容 适合用于 不太适合用于 链接 Matthew Henry Concise Commentary on the Whole Bible 十七世纪末写成的圣经注释 经典圣经解释 牧养和个人应用 讲道 历史证据研究 深入文本研究 Blue Letter Bible Sacred Texts 现代学习工具 整本圣经学习工具提供广泛而综合的圣经探索方式，常常汇集许多作者、学者和贡献者的内容。这些工具通常包括学习笔记、文章、地图、时间线、词语研究和主题指南等资源，帮助读者从多个角度理解圣经。许多资源现在可以在线使用，让人能快速进入大量资料，并进行更深入、更整合的学习。由于它们来自许多不同声音和视角，这类工具特别适合帮助人全面理解圣经。 名称 内容 适合用于 不太适合用于 类型 BibleRef.com 整本圣经 使用不同英文译本作单一解释 入门问题 文本分析 讲道 批判性研究 深入文本研究 逐节解释 BlueLetterBible.com 整本圣经 许多作者参与 多种译本 入门问题 文本分析 讲道 批判性研究 深入文本研究 快速参考 逐节解释 完整注释 希腊文/希伯来文行间工具 词语研究 主题研究 主题研究网站 下面的网站可以帮助你查找关于不同主题的更多资料。 名称 内容 适合用于 不太适合用于 类型 carm.org 按主题搜索 入门问题 研究 讲道 主题 gotquestions.org 按问题和主题搜索，圣经学习材料 入门问题 研究 主题式圣经学习 主题研究 主题式圣经学习

content: 福音 整本圣经都围绕一个简单而深刻的主题：上帝爱你，并为你开了一条路，使你的罪可以得赦免，并与他永远同在。这就是福音，也是圣经的中心。通过学习圣经，我们认识到每个人都需要被拯救（罗马书 3:23），每个人都可以被拯救（罗马书 1:16），而上帝也愿意人得救（彼得后书 3:9）。 使我们与上帝隔绝的是罪。无论我们觉得自己多么好，每个人都在罪中有份。上帝完全圣洁，所以我们无法靠努力、善行、金钱、才华或成就来除去自己的罪。幸运的是，上帝没有把我们留在与他隔绝的状态中，而是亲自开了一条修复关系的路。 这唯一的道路就是信靠耶稣基督。上帝亲自来到世上，成为人，过了完全无罪的生活，并甘愿为我们的罪付上代价。照圣经所说，凡信靠耶稣基督的人，都可以得赦免、得救，并有永恒的盼望。这不是盲目的相信，而是圣灵邀请我们信靠、顺服，并把自己交托给上帝。 得救不是靠人能“做”什么。人得救的唯一道路，是接受耶稣基督为救主。这意味着相信： 我是罪人，需要上帝的赦免。 耶稣基督是上帝，他来到世上成为人。 耶稣代替我死，为我的罪付上代价。 耶稣照他所说的从死里复活。 我信靠耶稣的牺牲，而不是靠自己得救。 我愿意离开罪，把信心放在耶稣身上。 这就是福音的核心。凡真心信靠耶稣的人，就已经得赦免，并开始从里面被改变。成为基督徒不是比别人更好，而是承认自己软弱、需要被拯救。圣经中的每一个重要主题，都指向罪、救赎，以及借着信心而来的救恩。 资料来源：The Gospel | BibleRef.com 和 Now what? | BibleRef.com 成为基督徒之后 “我刚成为基督徒！既然我已经信靠耶稣，现在该做什么？” 信靠基督是一个人能作出的最重要决定，也是一生学习和成长旅程的开始。这条路并不总是容易，但上帝应许与我们同在，并帮助我们继续前行。 一些重要的开始步骤包括： 1. 确认自己明白得救的决定。 圣经告诉我们，人可以知道自己是否真正得救。得救的核心是：人人都犯了罪；上帝圣洁公义；耶稣基督为我们的罪死，并从死里复活；凡承认自己的罪并信靠耶稣的人，就得赦免和救恩。 2. 与教导圣经的教会连接。 基督徒生活不是独自走的。我们需要其他信徒帮助我们理解圣经、彼此鼓励，也一起敬拜上帝。 3. 每天为上帝留出时间。 祷告和读圣经是属灵生命成长的重要部分。祷告不需要复杂或华丽，而是向上帝表达敬拜、需要、感谢和真实的心。读圣经帮助我们认识上帝的心意。 4. 建立帮助属灵成长的关系。 你与谁同行，会深深影响你的生命。基督徒之间的友谊、鼓励、陪伴和门徒训练，都能帮助信心更加稳固。 5. 顺服上帝，并思考洗礼。 洗礼不是得救的条件，也不是洗去罪的仪式；它是公开表达信心和顺服耶稣的一步。如果你已经真心接受耶稣为救主，可以和教会牧者谈谈洗礼。 写下和分享见证 写基督徒见证，是分享你与上帝同行故事的一种有意义方式。圣经没有要求每个人必须写见证，但这是一种很有帮助的工具，可以帮助你在传福音、洗礼或与朋友家人分享时，更清楚地表达自己的信仰。 你可以从以下几个部分整理自己的见证： 背景 我在怎样的文化、社会、属灵和家庭环境中长大？ 我过去如何看待生命和死亡？ 我过去对基督信仰知道多少？ 转变过程 是什么让我开始了解圣经、圣经中的上帝和基督信仰？ 是什么使我相信圣经中的上帝是真实的？ 耶稣在这个过程中扮演了什么角色？ 罪对我意味着什么？我为什么需要赦免？ 悔改对我意味着什么？我愿意怎样转向上帝？ 我是否想受洗？为什么？ 新的身份、世界观和期待 现在耶稣对我是谁？ 圣灵是谁，他如何在我的生命中工作？ 我的关系、价值观和人生方向有什么改变？ 我对永恒有什么盼望？ 我为什么感谢上帝？ 分享见证 对有些人来说，分享见证很自然；对另一些人来说，分享自己的生命故事会比较困难。当你有预备时，就更容易清楚分享，也更容易带来影响。 可以先思考五个问题： 在认识耶稣之前，我是谁？ 我是怎样认识他的？ 当我选择接受他的赦免时，发生了什么？ 我的生命从那以后有什么改变？ 信仰今天怎样影响我的生活？ 保持简单、真实、清楚。你可以准备一个较短版本和一个较长版本。最重要的是，这是你的故事。 我如何得救？ 这个问题假设你已经意识到自己需要被拯救。基督信仰的基础是：救恩只借着信靠耶稣基督而来。人要与上帝恢复关系，最重要的是接受这个真理：耶稣已经完成了一切必要的事，使你可以回到上帝面前。 上帝已经伸出他的手，你可以抓住他的手，离开罪和破碎。他会赐给你真实的身份，使你的思想被更新。你会成为新造的人，同时也越来越成为真正的自己。 真实的信心会带来改变。基督徒不是靠好行为换取上帝接纳，而是因为已经蒙恩，开始活出新的生命。过去以自我为中心的生活，会逐渐转向爱上帝、服事他人和关心群体。上帝也预备了好行为，让信徒在新的生命中去行。 有些人会问：如果只需要相信，那人是不是可以继续做坏事？圣经的回答是，真正的信心会结出生命改变的果子。保罗强调人是因信称义，不是靠行为；雅各强调真正的信心一定会在生活中显出好行为。他们并不矛盾，而是从不同角度说明同一个真理：得救是出于恩典，真实的信心会带来改变。

content: ANBI De Stichting Chinese Student Ministries Netherlands is ingeschreven bij de Kamer van Koophandel onder nummer 64512487. Het RSIN is 8556.98.469. De stichting heeft de ANBI status. Door deze status zijn giften aan de stichting aftrekbaar. Voor meer informatie hierover kan de website van de Belastingdienst worden geraadpleegd. Gegevens van de Stichting Naam: Chinese Student Ministries Netherlands Contactgegevens: Bert Verbeeke, Jan Slauerhoffstraat 17, 6708 RJ Wageningen, 06 19995615 Bestuur: voorzitter E. J. Bakker, secretaris J.G.W. Verbeeke Sterken, penningmeester M. Tolstead Beloningsbeleid: zoals vermeld in de statuten ontvangt het bestuur geen beloning voor de verrichte werkzaamheden. Doelstelling: Chinese studenten aan Nederlandse instellingen voor hoger onderwijs bekendmaken met het Evangelie en activiteiten verrichten die daarmee verband houden. content: CSMN Veelgestelde Vragen Wie is CSMN? CSMN staat voor Chinese Student Ministries Netherlands. We zijn een christelijke organisatie voor Chinese studenten en zijn officieel verbonden aan International Christian Fellowship (ICF). Wat doen we? We bieden een veilige en gastvrije plek waar studenten geloof kunnen verkennen, betekenisvolle vragen kunnen stellen, gemeenschap kunnen bouwen en samen kunnen groeien. Dit omvat regelmatige bijeenkomsten, gesprekken, aanbidding, sociale activiteiten en af en toe reizen of retraites. Wat doen we niet? We dwingen niemand om Jezus te volgen. We respecteren ieders reis en overtuigingen. Waarom specifiek Chinese studenten? Ons team heeft een bijzondere band met China. De meesten van ons hebben daar gewoond en voelen een sterke verbondenheid met de cultuur en de mensen. We willen dat Chinese studenten zich gezien, begrepen en thuis voelen in een land dat heel anders kan zijn dan hun eigen land. Ik ben geen christen. Kan ik meedoen? Ja. Studenten met alle achtergronden en wereldbeelden zijn welkom, of je nu nieuwsgierig bent, kritisch bent of gewoon geloof wilt verkennen en grote vragen wilt stellen. Wat kost lidmaatschap? Meedoen kost niets. Onze activiteiten en bijeenkomsten zijn gratis, tenzij bij een speciale activiteit of reis iets anders wordt vermeld. Wat kan ik verwachten? We streven naar een vriendelijke en respectvolle omgeving. Tijdens onze bijeenkomsten en activiteiten drinken we geen alcohol en roken we niet. Welke activiteiten doen jullie naast de vaste bijeenkomsten? Naast wekelijkse bijeenkomsten organiseren we: Wandelingen en natuuractiviteiten Filmavonden Sociale maaltijden Spelavonden Weekend retraites en kampen Hoe ziet een typische avond eruit? Een gewone avond bestaat uit: Welkom en informeel samenzijn Zingen of aanbidding, deelname is vrijwillig Een korte talk of discussie Groepsgesprek of reflectie Eten, snacks en sociale tijd Zijn jullie alleen voor protestanten? We zijn een protestants christelijke organisatie, maar studenten uit alle denominaties en met alle overtuigingen zijn van harte welkom.

content: Doe mee met CSMN Fellowship We nodigen je graag uit voor onze CSMN fellowship op vrijdagavond op onze vaste plek. Elke week komen we samen voor een warme en vrolijke avond met eten, vriendschap en gemeenschap. We beginnen om 18:00 met een heerlijke Chinese maaltijd die we samen delen. Het is een mooie gelegenheid om goed te eten, bekende gezichten weer te zien en nieuwe Chinese studenten welkom te heten die zich hebben aangemeld. Om genoeg eten voor iedereen te kunnen voorbereiden, vragen we je om je vooraf aan te melden. Je aanmelding helpt ons goed te plannen en voor iedere gast te zorgen. Na de maaltijd eten we vaak verjaardagstaart of een speciaal dessert om iets betekenisvols te vieren. Met koffie, thee, frisdrank of water gaan we verder met samen zingen, gevolgd door een studie. Elke week gaat de studie over een thema dat ons helpt om het leven dieper en bewuster te ontdekken. Voor nieuwkomers is er ook een speciale introductiegroep, zodat je ons stap voor stap kunt leren kennen en je op je gemak kunt voelen. Je kunt je hier aanmelden: events. Kom erbij en word onderdeel van een mooie gemeenschap. Goed eten, betekenisvolle gesprekken en nieuwe vriendschappen wachten op je. We kijken ernaar uit je vrijdag te zien!

content: Bijbelstudie Het christelijk geloof wordt op veel verschillende manieren uitgedrukt. Soms lijken deze vormen en praktijken tegenover elkaar te staan, alsof elke traditie zelf wil bepalen wat het christelijk geloof is. Voor iemand die nieuw is in het christelijk geloof kan dit verwarring en vragen oproepen. Er is geen simpele verklaring voor de diversiteit onder christelijke kerken. Zelfs als we elk verschil bestuderen en proberen tegengestelde standpunten met elkaar te verzoenen, blijft volledige eenheid buiten bereik. De wereld is simpelweg zeer divers, en de menselijke natuur, met haar verlangen naar eigenheid en haar hardnekkigheid, maakt volledige eenheid moeilijk. Gelukkig zijn er binnen deze grote diversiteit een aantal gedeelde kern overtuigingen. Deze gemeenschappelijke basis komt sterk naar voren in de Apostolische Geloofsbelijdenis, die de kern samenvat van wat christenen wereldwijd belijden. Verschillende tradities kunnen verschillende accenten leggen, maar er blijft brede en blijvende overeenstemming over de wezenlijke waarheden van het geloof en over de noodzaak om deze centrale overtuigingen samen vast te houden. Om de harmonie binnen deze diversiteit te waarderen, moeten we zoeken naar een diepere waarheid: de waarheid dat Gods liefde kan schijnen in elke unieke context. Bij CSMN nodigen we deelnemers uit om de rijkdom en variatie in verschillende christelijke tradities te ontdekken. We begrijpen deze uitdrukkingen als contextuele verschijningsvormen van Gods liefde in de wereld. De manier waarop Gods liefde lang geleden zichtbaar werd, is niet identiek aan hoe zij in de eenentwintigste eeuw wordt uitgedrukt. Toch is Gods liefde zelf nooit veranderd; zijn passie voor mensen blijft dezelfde. De Schrift bewaart deze uitdrukkingen van Gods liefde voor ons. De verhalen over hoe God door de geschiedenis heen met mensen omging, zijn verzameld in de canon van de Hebreeuwse Bijbel en het Nieuwe Testament. Deze canon is gesloten en stabiel gebleven, en is al bijna tweeduizend jaar de fundamentele referentie voor christenen. Omdat de Bijbel ons belangrijkste “leerboek” is, leggen we veel nadruk op het bestuderen ervan. Door de Schrift leren we hoe God zich door de eeuwen heen heeft geopenbaard en hoe eerdere generaties Hem leerden kennen. We verankeren ons denken bewust in de openbaring die God al gegeven heeft. Het materiaal op onze site wordt op verschillende manieren gebruikt. Sommige materialen zijn door ons geschreven en andere zijn geleend of aanbevolen. We vermelden waar mogelijk de bron en linken naar het origineel of naar de plek waar het gekocht kan worden. Online Bijbelcommentaren Een commentaar op de Bijbel, of op een specifiek Bijbelboek, is een verzameling artikelen van geleerden of aandachtige lezers die inzicht geven in de tekst. Commentaren bieden frisse perspectieven en behandelen vaak vragen zoals wie de tekst schreef, wanneer die geschreven werd en met welk doel. Ze leggen de betekenis van de tekst uit voor het oorspronkelijke publiek en helpen ons begrijpen hoe die inzichten vandaag kunnen worden toegepast. Omdat er een lange geschiedenis van Bijbelcommentaren is, is het belangrijk betrouwbare bronnen te kiezen. Hieronder vind je materialen die we in het verleden hebben gebruikt of nog steeds gebruiken wanneer dat passend is. Traditionele commentaren Traditionele Bijbelcommentaren zijn gerichte verklaringen van de Bijbel, geschreven door een specifieke auteur om de betekenis van de tekst uit te leggen en toe te passen op het dagelijks leven. In tegenstelling tot uitgebreide studietools die de hele Bijbel behandelen met allerlei functies, geven deze commentaren een meer geconcentreerde blik op de tekst. Ze bieden vaak historische achtergrond, theologische reflectie en vers voor vers inzicht. De focus ligt meer op prediking en op wat het betekent om je aan Jezus over te geven. Gebruik dit materiaal om snel een indruk te krijgen van wat een bepaalde passage inhoudt. Vaak brengen ze het werk samen van veel auteurs, geleerden en bijdragers. Deze tools bevatten meestal allerlei bronnen, zoals studienotities, artikelen, kaarten, tijdlijnen, woordstudies en thematische gidsen, om lezers te helpen de Bijbel vanuit meerdere invalshoeken te begrijpen. Veel van deze bronnen zijn online beschikbaar, waardoor je snel toegang krijgt tot grote bibliotheken met informatie en dieper, meer geïntegreerd kunt studeren. content: Het Evangelie De hele Bijbel draait om één eenvoudig maar diepgaand thema: God houdt zoveel van je dat Hij een weg heeft gemaakt waardoor je zonden vergeven kunnen worden en je eeuwig met Hem kunt leven. Dat is de kern van het evangelie en het centrale onderwerp van de Schrift. Door de Bijbel te bestuderen leren we dat ieder mens gered moet worden (Romeinen 3:23), ieder mens gered kan worden (Romeinen 1:16) en God wil dat mensen gered worden (2 Petrus 3:9). Wat ons van God scheidt, is zonde. Hoe goed we onszelf ook vinden, ieder mens heeft gezondigd. Omdat God volmaakt heilig is, kunnen inspanning, goede daden, geld, talent of prestaties onze schuld niet wegnemen. Gelukkig wil God niet dat wij van Hem gescheiden blijven. Daarom heeft Hij zelf een weg gemaakt om te herstellen wat gebroken is. Die enige weg is geloof in Jezus Christus. God kwam zelf naar de aarde als mens, leefde een volmaakt en zondeloos leven, en stierf vrijwillig om de schuld van onze zonden te dragen. Volgens de Schrift kan iedereen die op Jezus Christus vertrouwt, vergeving en redding ontvangen. Dit is geen oproep tot blind geloof, maar een uitnodiging van de Heilige Geest tot vertrouwen, overgave en gehoorzaamheid. Er is niets wat iemand kan “doen” om zichzelf te redden. De enige weg naar redding is Jezus Christus aannemen als Redder. Dat betekent geloven dat: ik een zondaar ben en Gods vergeving nodig heb; Jezus Christus God is en als mens naar de aarde kwam; Jezus in mijn plaats stierf om voor mijn zonden te betalen; Jezus uit de dood opstond, zoals Hij gezegd had; ik vertrouw op Jezus’ offer en niet op mijzelf; ik mij afkeer van mijn zonde en mijn geloof op Jezus stel. Dat is de kern van het evangelie. Wie werkelijk op Jezus vertrouwt, ontvangt vergeving en begint van binnenuit te veranderen. Christen worden betekent niet dat je beter bent dan anderen. Het betekent dat je erkent dat je zwak bent en redding nodig hebt. De grote thema’s van de Schrift wijzen steeds weer naar zonde, verlossing en redding door geloof. Bronnen: The Gospel | BibleRef.com en Now what? | BibleRef.com Nadat je christen bent geworden “Ik ben net christen geworden! Nu ik mijn geloof in Jezus heb gesteld, wat doe ik nu?” Op Christus vertrouwen is de belangrijkste beslissing die iemand kan nemen. Het is ook het begin van een levenslange weg van groei en leren. Die weg is niet altijd makkelijk, maar God belooft met ons mee te gaan en ons te helpen. Een paar belangrijke eerste stappen zijn: 1. Begrijp de beslissing die je hebt genomen. De Bijbel zegt dat we mogen weten of we werkelijk gered zijn. De kern is: iedereen heeft gezondigd; God is heilig en goed; Jezus Christus stierf voor onze zonden en stond op uit de dood; wie zijn zonde erkent en op Jezus vertrouwt, ontvangt vergeving en redding. 2. Verbind je met een kerk waar de Bijbel wordt onderwezen. Het christelijk leven is niet bedoeld om alleen te leven. We hebben andere gelovigen nodig om de Bijbel beter te begrijpen, elkaar te bemoedigen en samen God te aanbidden. 3. Neem dagelijks tijd voor God. Gebed en Bijbellezen zijn belangrijk voor geestelijke groei. Gebed hoeft niet ingewikkeld of mooi geformuleerd te zijn. Het is de plek waar we God aanbidden, onze zorgen bij Hem brengen, danken en vragen om wat we nodig hebben. Door de Bijbel te lezen leren we Gods wil kennen. 4. Bouw relaties op die helpen bij geestelijke groei. De mensen met wie je optrekt, hebben veel invloed op je leven. Christelijke vriendschap, bemoediging, begeleiding en discipelschap helpen je geloof steviger te worden. 5. Volg Gods wil en denk na over de doop. De doop is geen voorwaarde voor redding en geen ritueel dat zonden lichamelijk wegwast. Het is een openbare stap van gehoorzaamheid: een manier om je geloof in Christus zichtbaar te maken. Als je Jezus oprecht als Redder hebt aangenomen, kun je met een voorganger of leider praten over de doop. Getuigenis schrijven en delen Een christelijk getuigenis schrijven is een betekenisvolle manier om het verhaal van je persoonlijke weg met God te delen. Het is geen bijbelse verplichting, maar wel een nuttig hulpmiddel om je geloof duidelijk te verwoorden, bijvoorbeeld bij evangelisatie, een doopdienst of een persoonlijk gesprek met vrienden en familie. Je kunt je getuigenis opbouwen rond deze onderdelen: Achtergrond Waar en hoe ben ik opgegroeid, cultureel, sociaal, geestelijk en politiek? Hoe keek ik naar leven en dood? Wat wist ik over het christelijk geloof? Proces van bekering Wat maakte dat ik de Bijbel, de God van de Bijbel en het christelijk geloof ging onderzoeken? Wat overtuigde mij dat de God van de Bijbel echt is? Welke rol had Jezus hierin? Wat betekent zonde voor mij? Waarom heb ik vergeving nodig? Wat betekent bekering voor mij? Wil ik van richting veranderen? Wil ik gedoopt worden? Waarom wel of niet? Mijn nieuwe status, wereldbeeld en verwachtingen Wie is Jezus voor mij? Wie is de Heilige Geest en waar is Hij in mijn leven? Wat verandert er in mijn relaties, waarden en richting? Wat is mijn bestemming in de eeuwigheid? Waar ben ik God dankbaar voor? Getuigenis delen Voor sommige mensen voelt het natuurlijk om hun getuigenis te delen. Voor anderen is het moeilijker om hun levensverhaal te vertellen. Als je voorbereid bent, wordt het makkelijker om helder te delen. Denk bijvoorbeeld na over vijf vragen: Wie was ik voordat ik Jezus leerde kennen? Hoe heb ik Hem leren kennen? Wat gebeurde er toen ik zijn vergeving ontving? Hoe is mijn leven sindsdien veranderd? Welke invloed heeft mijn geloof vandaag op mijn leven? Houd het eenvoudig, eerlijk en duidelijk. Je kunt een korte en een langere versie voorbereiden. Boven alles: dit is jouw verhaal. Hoe word ik gered? Deze vraag veronderstelt dat je inziet dat je redding nodig hebt. De basis van het christelijk geloof is dat redding alleen komt door geloof in Jezus Christus. Het belangrijkste is deze waarheid te aanvaarden: Jezus heeft alles gedaan wat nodig is om de relatie tussen jou en God te herstellen. God heeft zijn hand al uitgestoken. Jij mag die hand vastgrijpen en uit zonde en gebrokenheid worden opgetild. Hij geeft je een echte identiteit en vernieuwt je denken. In deze nieuwe identiteit word je een nieuwe schepping, terwijl je juist steeds meer de echte jij wordt. Echt geloof brengt verandering. Christenen doen geen goede werken om Gods acceptatie te verdienen, maar omdat zij al genade hebben ontvangen en nieuw leven krijgen. Een leven dat eerst op jezelf gericht was, verandert langzaam in een leven dat God liefheeft, anderen dient en zorg draagt voor de gemeenschap. God bereidt ook goede werken voor die gelovigen mogen doen. Sommige mensen vragen: als je alleen hoeft te geloven, kun je dan gewoon doorgaan met slechte dingen doen? De Bijbel antwoordt dat echt geloof vrucht draagt in een veranderd leven. Paulus benadrukt dat mensen door geloof gerechtvaardigd worden en niet door werken. Jakobus benadrukt dat echt geloof zichtbaar wordt in goede werken. Zij spreken elkaar niet tegen, maar belichten dezelfde waarheid vanuit verschillende kanten: redding is genade, en echt geloof verandert een leven.

content:
I Will Be There The song I Will Be There (originally Ik zal er zijn) was born where hopelessness meets promise. Our singer at the time was diagnosed with incurable cancer; this song was our response. Since its release in Dutch in 2013, Ik zal er zijn has become an anthem of hope for anyone facing death or despair. You can hear it sung in services and gatherings throughout the Netherlands.

We are the Dutch band Sela. In this time of international fear and doubt we share our English language version of Ik zal er zijn in the hope that it could be as encouraging to a wider audience as it has been in our country.

At the end of the song you can hear voices from the Netherlands, the US, Canada, England, and Indonesia. Please sing with them and with us, as we celebrate the heart of God: “My name is I am, and I will be there.”

title: 唯独基督 In Christ Alone
description:

“In Christ Alone” is a popular modern Christian song written by Keith Getty and Stuart Townend, both songwriters of Christian hymns and contemporary worship music in the United Kingdom...
content:
唯独基督 In Christ Alone English Chinese 中文
“In Christ Alone” is a popular modern Christian song written by Keith Getty and Stuart Townend, both songwriters of Christian hymns and contemporary worship music in the United Kingdom. The song, with a strong Irish melody, is the first hymn they penned together. The music was by Getty and the original lyrics by Townend. It was composed in 2001. “In Christ Alone” is considered a Christian credal song for belief in Jesus Christ. The theme of the song is the life, death and resurrection of Christ, and that he is God whom even death cannot hold. The song is commonly known as “In Christ Alone (My Hope Is Found)” and “In Christ Alone (I Stand)” taking verses from the song. It has become very popular and has been the subject of many cover versions and many language translations.
Book of Ephesian：Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in the heavenly realms with every spiritual blessing in Christ. For he chose us in him before the creation of the world to be holy and blameless in his sight. In love he predestined us for adoption to sonship through Jesus Christ, in accordance with his pleasure and will — to the praise of his glorious grace, which he has freely given us in the One he loves. In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of God’s grace that he lavished on us. With all wisdom and understanding, 9 he made known to us the mystery of his will according to his good pleasure, which he purposed in Christ, to be put into effect when the times reach their fulfillment — to bring unity to all things in heaven and on earth under Christ. 这首诗歌即 Getty’s Music 的作品，英格兰诗歌作家 Stuart Townend 和现居美国田纳西州音乐之都的北爱尔兰著名作曲家 Keith Getty 试图创作兼具神学深度和诗词意境，音乐风格连接传统和现代，适合每一代人的圣诗。他们认为圣诗应教导整全圣经真理，同时又能深入人心，帮助基督徒反思和坚固信仰，建立他们的生命。《惟有基督》是两人2001年的首度合作，反响巨大。英国赞美诗协会认为《惟有基督》为有史以来最优秀的五首赞美诗之一。这首歌揉合了爱尔兰民谣曲调及现代音乐的风格，概略地勾勒了基督福音，自道成肉身起，陈明祂自取卑微、受苦担罪、得胜死亡等关于福音的基本轮廓。对华人基督徒而言，需稍加提醒的是，这首诗歌与约书亚乐团的同名歌曲〈耶稣基督〉（In Christ Alone）并不是同一首诗歌。
圣经以弗所书经文：
愿颂赞归与我们主耶稣基督的父神，他在基督里，曾赐给我们天上各样属灵的福气。就如神从创立世界以前，在基督里拣选了我们，使我们在他面前成为圣洁，无有瑕疵。又因爱我们，就按着自己意旨所喜悦的，预定我们，借着耶稣基督得儿子的名分，使他荣耀的恩典得着称赞。这恩典是他在爱子里所赐给我们的。我们借这爱子的血，得蒙救赎，过犯得以赦免，乃是照他丰富的恩典。这恩典是神用诸般智慧聪明，充充足足赏给我们的，都是照他自己所预定的美意，叫我们知道他旨意的奥秘，要照所安排的，在日期满足的时候，使天上地上一切所有 Chinese Worship

I Will Be There The song I Will Be There (originally Ik zal er zijn) was born where hopelessness meets promise. Our singer at the time was diagnosed with incurable cancer; this song was our response. Since its release in Dutch in 2013, Ik zal er zijn has become an anthem of hope for anyone facing death or despair. You can hear it sung in services and gatherings throughout the Netherlands.

We are the Dutch band Sela. In this time of international fear and doubt we share our English language version of Ik zal er zijn in the hope that it could be as encouraging to a wider audience as it has been in our country.

At the end of the song you can hear voices from the Netherlands, the US, Canada, England, and Indonesia. Please sing with them and with us, as we celebrate the heart of God: “My name is I am, and I will be there.”

title: 唯独基督 In Christ Alone
description:
English Chinese 中文
“In Christ Alone” is a popular modern Christian song written by Keith Getty and Stuart Townend, both songwriters of Christian hymns and contemporary worship music in the United Kingdom...
content:
唯独基督 In Christ Alone English Chinese 中文
“In Christ Alone” is a popular modern Christian song written by Keith Getty and Stuart Townend, both songwriters of Christian hymns and contemporary worship music in the United Kingdom. The song, with a strong Irish melody, is the first hymn they penned together. The music was by Getty and the original lyrics by Townend. It was composed in 2001. “In Christ Alone” is considered a Christian credal song for belief in Jesus Christ. The theme of the song is the life, death and resurrection of Christ, and that he is God whom even death cannot hold. The song is commonly known as “In Christ Alone (My Hope Is Found)” and “In Christ Alone (I Stand)” taking verses from the song. It has become very popular and has been the subject of many cover versions and many language translations.
Book of Ephesian：Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in the heavenly realms with every spiritual blessing in Christ. For he chose us in him before the creation of the world to be holy and blameless in his sight. In love he predestined us for adoption to sonship through Jesus Christ, in accordance with his pleasure and will — to the praise of his glorious grace, which he has freely given us in the One he loves. In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of God’s grace that he lavished on us. With all wisdom and understanding, 9 he made known to us the mystery of his will according to his good pleasure, which he purposed in Christ, to be put into effect when the times reach their fulfillment — to bring unity to all things in heaven and on earth under Christ. 这首诗歌即 Getty’s Music 的作品，英格兰诗歌作家 Stuart Townend 和现居美国田纳西州音乐之都的北爱尔兰著名作曲家 Keith Getty 试图创作兼具神学深度和诗词意境，音乐风格连接传统和现代，适合每一代人的圣诗。他们认为圣诗应教导整全圣经真理，同时又能深入人心，帮助基督徒反思和坚固信仰，建立他们的生命。《惟有基督》是两人2001年的首度合作，反响巨大。英国赞美诗协会认为《惟有基督》为有史以来最优秀的五首赞美诗之一。这首歌揉合了爱尔兰民谣曲调及现代音乐的风格，概略地勾勒了基督福音，自道成肉身起，陈明祂自取卑微、受苦担罪、得胜死亡等关于福音的基本轮廓。对华人基督徒而言，需稍加提醒的是，这首诗歌与约书亚乐团的同名歌曲〈耶稣基督〉（In Christ Alone）并不是同一首诗歌。
圣经以弗所书经文：
愿颂赞归与我们主耶稣基督的父神，他在基督里，曾赐给我们天上各样属灵的福气。就如神从创立世界以前，在基督里拣选了我们，使我们在他面前成为圣洁，无有瑕疵。又因爱我们，就按着自己意旨所喜悦的，预定我们，借着耶稣基督得儿子的名分，使他荣耀的恩典得着称赞。这恩典是他在爱子里所赐给我们的。我们借这爱子的血，得蒙救赎，过犯得以赦免，乃是照他丰富的恩典。这恩典是神用诸般智慧聪明，充充足足赏给我们的，都是照他自己所预定的美意，叫我们知道他旨意的奥秘，要照所安排的，在日期满足的时候，使天上地上一切所有 Chinese Worship

Faithful One Experience the timeless declaration of God's faithfulness through Brian Doerksen's powerful worship anthem "Faithful One." This beloved modern hymn has become a cornerstone of contemporary Christian worship, perfectly expressing our trust in God's unchanging nature.

## Song Message
"Faithful One" centers on God's unwavering faithfulness and dependability in every season of life. The lyrics emphasize personal trust in God's consistent character while acknowledging His role as our firm foundation.

## Historical Background
- Released in 1996 on Doerksen's album "Faithful"
- Written by Brian Doerksen while serving at Vineyard Churches in the UK
- Inspired by God's faithfulness during a challenging season in the songwriter's life
- Became widely popular in churches globally through Vineyard Worship movement English Worship

description: The song I Will Be There (originally Ik zal er zijn) was born where hopelessness meets promise. Our singer at the time was diagnosed with incurable cancer; this song was our response...
content:
I Will Be There The song I Will Be There (originally Ik zal er zijn) was born where hopelessness meets promise. Our singer at the time was diagnosed with incurable cancer; this song was our response. Since its release in Dutch in 2013, Ik zal er zijn has become an anthem of hope for anyone facing death or despair. You can hear it sung in services and gatherings throughout the Netherlands.

We are the Dutch band Sela. In this time of international fear and doubt we share our English language version of Ik zal er zijn in the hope that it could be as encouraging to a wider audience as it has been in our country.

At the end of the song you can hear voices from the Netherlands, the US, Canada, England, and Indonesia. Please sing with them and with us, as we celebrate the heart of God: “My name is I am, and I will be there.”

Lyrics: Hans Maat Music: Kinga Bán and Adrian Roest

Standing before a burning bush, Moses asked, “Who are you?” God answered, “I AM WHO I AM.” This name declares God's eternal, unchanging nature—He exists beyond time and space, from before the beginning to forever.

Later, standing before religious leaders, Jesus said, “Before Abraham was, I AM.” With these words, He revealed Himself as Yahweh in the flesh, converging with humanity to redeem the whole earth in a way nobody could have expected.

This claim shattered the mindsets of so many, as Jesus proclaimed that He was and is Yahweh, the Great I AM, who was, and is, and is to come. He is always with us. His existence never ends, His mercy never fails and His praises will echo throughout eternity. Yahweh, the Great I AM is worthy of all praise now and evermore.

title: 唯独基督 In Christ Alone
description:
English Chinese 中文
“In Christ Alone” is a popular modern Christian song written by Keith Getty and Stuart Townend, both songwriters of Christian hymns and contemporary worship music in the United Kingdom...
content:
唯独基督 In Christ Alone English Chinese 中文
“In Christ Alone” is a popular modern Christian song written by Keith Getty and Stuart Townend, both songwriters of Christian hymns and contemporary worship music in the United Kingdom. The song, with a strong Irish melody, is the first hymn they penned together. The music was by Getty and the original lyrics by Townend. It was composed in 2001. “In Christ Alone” is considered a Christian credal song for belief in Jesus Christ. The theme of the song is the life, death and resurrection of Christ, and that he is God whom even death cannot hold. The song is commonly known as “In Christ Alone (My Hope Is Found)” and “In Christ Alone (I Stand)” taking verses from the song. It has become very popular and has been the subject of many cover versions and many language translations.
Book of Ephesian：Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in the heavenly realms with every spiritual blessing in Christ. For he chose us in him before the creation of the world to be holy and blameless in his sight. In love he predestined us for adoption to sonship through Jesus Christ, in accordance with his pleasure and will — to the praise of his glorious grace, which he has freely given us in the One he loves. In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of God’s grace that he lavished on us. With all wisdom and understanding, 9 he made known to us the mystery of his will according to his good pleasure, which he purposed in Christ, to be put into effect when the times reach their fulfillment — to bring unity to all things in heaven and on earth under Christ. 这首诗歌即 Getty’s Music 的作品，英格兰诗歌作家 Stuart Townend 和现居美国田纳西州音乐之都的北爱尔兰著名作曲家 Keith Getty 试图创作兼具神学深度和诗词意境，音乐风格连接传统和现代，适合每一代人的圣诗。他们认为圣诗应教导整全圣经真理，同时又能深入人心，帮助基督徒反思和坚固信仰，建立他们的生命。《惟有基督》是两人2001年的首度合作，反响巨大。英国赞美诗协会认为《惟有基督》为有史以来最优秀的五首赞美诗之一。这首歌揉合了爱尔兰民谣曲调及现代音乐的风格，概略地勾勒了基督福音，自道成肉身起，陈明祂自取卑微、受苦担罪、得胜死亡等关于福音的基本轮廓。对华人基督徒而言，需稍加提醒的是，这首诗歌与约书亚乐团的同名歌曲〈耶稣基督〉（In Christ Alone）并不是同一首诗歌。
圣经以弗所书经文：
愿颂赞归与我们主耶稣基督的父神，他在基督里，曾赐给我们天上各样属灵的福气。就如神从创立世界以前，在基督里拣选了我们，使我们在他面前成为圣洁，无有瑕疵。又因爱我们，就按着自己意旨所喜悦的，预定我们，借着耶稣基督得儿子的名分，使他荣耀的恩典得着称赞。这恩典是他在爱子里所赐给我们的。我们借这爱子的血，得蒙救赎，过犯得以赦免，乃是照他丰富的恩典。这恩典是神用诸般智慧聪明，充充足足赏给我们的，都是照他自己所预定的美意，叫我们知道他旨意的奥秘，要照所安排的，在日期满足的时候，使天上地上一切所有 Chinese Worship
